question.text: An NPO's tax exemption and donor tax-benefit status are granted under which sections of the Income Tax Act 1961?

answer.text: Section 12A/12AB (registration for tax exemption) and Section 80G (donor deduction eligibility)
Section 10(23C) only; no other sections are relevant
Section 11 (application of income) and Section 35AC (scientific research)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.8.1 (B)(4), NPOs get tax exemption under Section 12A/12AB, and donors get deductions under Section 80G. These are the two primary IT-Act routes discussed in Ch 1. Section 11 deals with application of income (85%) and 10(23C) with specific exempt institutions — but the primary pair is 12AB + 80G. The Trap: Option A is wrong — 135 is Companies Act (not IT Act), 115BBI is anonymous-donation penalty. Option C narrows excessively. Option D mixes 11 and 35AC which are tangential. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 10 (Taxation — full chapter), V-A (MF Distributor 80G), X-A (Investment Adviser). For SIAs, 12AB validity is a precondition for certifying the NPO's tax-exempt outflows. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Request the 12AB registration certificate (not just 12A — 12A was replaced by 12AB via the Finance Act 2020). Validity is 5 years; approaching expiry is a going-concern risk. Flag in SAS-100 management letter.
